description: Fig. 22 is a four-panel composite (a–d) of simulation output from an inhomogeneous-dislocation-density 3D cellular automaton (CA) model of low-alloy steel, plotted as line curves. No image pixels were supplied with this request, so the following is reconstructed from the caption and citing text only and the panels could not be read directly. (a) and (c) plot DRX fraction and average dislocation density, respectively, versus true strain for a transiently increasing strain rate from 0.01 s^-1 to 0.1 s^-1 at 950 °C applied at 0.2 or 0.4 strain. (b) and (d) plot the same two quantities for decreasing temperature from 1050 °C to 950 °C in strain ranges 0.2–0.3 or 0.4–0.5 at 0.01 s^-1. Curves in (a, b) are labelled Total, First stage and Second stage; curves in (c, d) are labelled Matrix grains, DRXGs_I and DRXGs_II. Axis ranges, tick values, line colours and any printed numbers cannot be verified. The figure argues that a transient rise in Z_P generates a second DRX-grain population, DRXGs_II, whose lower dislocation density promotes refinement of the matrix and of the first-stage DRXGs.

observations.observation: Fig. 22 is a four-panel set (a)–(d) plotting DRX fraction (a, b) and average dislocation density (c, d) against true strain for CA simulations of transiently increasing Z_P.
Panels (a) and (c) correspond to a transiently increasing strain rate from 0.01 s^-1 to 0.1 s^-1 at 950 °C applied at 0.2 or 0.4 strain.
Panels (b) and (d) correspond to decreasing temperature from 1050 °C to 950 °C in strain ranges of 0.2–0.3 or 0.4–0.5 at 0.01 s^-1.
Curve families in the DRX-fraction panels are labelled Total, First stage and Second stage.
Curve families in the average-dislocation-density panels are labelled Matrix grains, DRXGs_I and DRXGs_II.

The citing text states that the DRX fraction in the second stage began to increase significantly only after a delay, especially when the strain rate was transiently increased, and that the rise relied mostly on growth of DRXGs_II (termed 'pseudo-metadynamic recrystallization').
The citing text states that the DRX fraction of the first stage gradually decreased as the second-stage DRX fraction increased, indicating DRXGs_II refined both the matrix and the DRXGs_I.

The citing text states that the critical dislocation density increased with Z_P elevation, delaying nucleation of DRXGs_II, so the total DRX fraction late in the second stage stayed lower than under the corresponding constant deformation condition.
The citing text states that the average dislocation density of DRXGs_II was lower than that of both the matrix and DRXGs_I, providing the driving force for refinement seen in the DRX-fraction panels.
No printed numeric values, axis tick labels, or line styles could be confirmed because image pixels were not provided with this request.
